source.title: The organization of recent and remote memories.

confidence_rationale: Canonical NRN review; strong source quality. Maps onto the multi-STATE-over-time premise behind MECH-391's lifecycle store (recent hippocampus-dependent -> remote cortical), but does not itself specify a 6-label taxonomy or an allocation-decision policy, so mapping_fidelity is held mid.
failure_signatures: The review establishes that memories pass through distinct, time-dependent states with different anatomical substrates, but it does not enumerate discrete lifecycle LABELS (retained/indexed/summarised/consolidated/contested/retired) nor describe a control-plane that decides among them -- the staging is observed, the policy is a REE overlay.

mapping.source_claim_statement: New episodic memories initially depend on the medial temporal lobe / hippocampus and, as they mature, become increasingly dependent on distributed cortical networks; the transformation from recent to remote memory is a staged, molecularly and cellularly distinct process.
mapping.ree_translation: The biological warrant for MECH-391 treating memory as a multi-STATE lifecycle rather than a single store: a trace occupies time-dependent states (indexed in hippocampus -> consolidated in cortex) with different substrate homes, which is precisely the premise a lifecycle store with distinct state labels operationalises.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Frankland & Bontempi ground that there ARE distinct time-dependent memory states; they do NOT ground REE's specific 6-state vocabulary nor the allocation-gate decision (integrate/partial_overlap/separate). The staging is descriptive biology; the discrete-state model and the control policy remain REE design choices.
mapping.source_context: Review of rodent + human systems-consolidation literature (lesion, imaging, molecular).

confidence_components.notes: High venue/source quality; mapping held mid because the paper grounds the staging premise, not the discrete-state taxonomy or the policy.
